summary: Implementation of observability layer: 11 built-in action functions, HookWatcher with fsnotify, Unix socket action endpoints, LinuxSystemReader, JournalctlReader, FileSource, LogFilter, AgentStatsCollector, and CLI commands. All tests pass with -race. 4 of 11 built-in actions are wired in up.go; 7 remain unregistered due to missing provider implementations at the wiring layer. FileSource is implemented but not wired. CLI commands lack HTTP status code validation.

tests_checklist.item: Built-in actions have happy path + error tests
HookWatcher has lifecycle tests with goleak
FileSource tests cover glob, truncation, rotation
LogFilter tests cover severity, unit-include, unit-exclude, combination
SystemReader tests pass on Linux with real /proc
Integration tests verify action server + watcher lifecycle
Edge cases tested: empty, null, boundary values

code_quality_checklist.item: Follows existing code patterns (interface injection, Config+ApplyDefaults)
Error messages follow 'package: context: detail' convention
Clean shutdown behavior for all goroutines
CLI commands check HTTP status codes before parsing (pattern from state.go)

security_checklist.item: Hook names validated against path traversal
Command injection prevented via net.ParseIP for traceroute/ping targets
Hook integrity verified via SHA-256 before execution
Request body size limited with MaxBytesReader
Parameter sanitization for hook environment variables
Report key validated against path traversal
LogsSnapshot lines parameter has upper bound

architecture_checklist.item: Platform-specific code isolated with build tags
All new components properly wired in up.go

fail_fast_checklist.item: Invalid input rejected with clear messages

defensive_checklist.item: Panic recovery in action execution and log collection

security_findings.description: LogsSnapshot action accepts unbounded 'lines' parameter. An attacker requesting lines=999999999 could cause memory exhaustion via the LogProvider.
security_findings.fix: Add max cap: const maxLogSnapshotLines = 10000; if parsed > maxLogSnapshotLines { n = maxLogSnapshotLines }

architecture_findings.description: 7 of 11 built-in actions are implemented in builtins.go but NOT registered with the Executor in up.go. Missing: gather_info, ping, diagnostics.traceroute_peer, health.check, mesh.reconnect, config.dump, logs.snapshot. These require provider interfaces (NodeInfoProvider, HealthProvider, MeshReconnector, ConfigProvider, LogProvider) that are not wired at the application level. The functions exist and have tests, but they are unreachable at runtime.
architecture_findings.fix: Register all 11 built-in actions. For actions requiring providers, either implement the provider adapters wrapping existing agent state (e.g. identity for NodeInfoProvider, heartbeat for HealthProvider), or register with nil-safe stubs that return 'provider not configured' until the full agent state is available.

architecture_findings.description: FileSource is fully implemented with glob support, offset tracking, rotation detection, and 16 KiB truncation but is never wired into the log forwarder in up.go. The Config struct has no field for file-based log source patterns. Plan task 5.1 says 'Add FileSource ... to log forwarder when configured' but this was not done.
architecture_findings.fix: Add a FilePatterns []string field to logfwd.Config (or agent.Config.LogFwd), iterate patterns in up.go to create FileSource instances, and register them with logForwarder.RegisterSource().

issues_found.description: 7 of 11 built-in actions not registered. gather_info, ping, diagnostics.traceroute_peer, health.check, mesh.reconnect, config.dump, logs.snapshot are implemented but unreachable.
issues_found.fix: Register all actions with appropriate provider adapters. For NodeInfoProvider, wrap identity. For HealthProvider, create adapter from heartbeat service. For MeshReconnector, wrap tunnel manager. For ConfigProvider, implement config sanitizer. For LogProvider, wrap ring buffer or journald.

issues_found.description: FileSource not wired in up.go. Fully implemented but no configuration path exists to enable file-based log collection.
issues_found.fix: Add file source patterns to Config, create FileSource instances in up.go for each pattern, register with forwarder.

issues_found.description: CLI commands do not check HTTP status codes before parsing response body. Existing pattern in state.go checks StatusCode for all responses. On error responses (500, 503), the CLI will attempt to unmarshal error JSON into expected struct, producing confusing errors.
issues_found.fix: Add status code check after each socketGet/socketPost call: if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK { body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body); return fmt.Errorf(...unexpected status %d: %s..., resp.StatusCode, body) }

issues_found.description: LogsSnapshot accepts unbounded 'lines' parameter (any positive int). No test for boundary values like lines=0, lines=-1, lines=maxint.
issues_found.fix: Add const maxLogSnapshotLines = 10000 and clamp. Add tests for boundary values.

issues_found.description: processFileLocked is misleadingly named - it acquires the lock internally rather than requiring the caller to hold it. Comment on line 256 says 'no onChange call, caller holds no lock'.
issues_found.fix: Rename to processFileInitial or processFileForScan to clarify that it handles its own locking.

issues_found.description: Documentation describes all 11 built-in actions as available, but only 4 are actually registered and usable. Users following the docs will encounter 'unknown builtin action' errors for 7 actions.
issues_found.fix: Either register all actions (preferred) or add 'Not yet wired - requires provider implementation' notes to the 7 unregistered action docs.

suggested_improvements: Add stack trace to panic recovery in executor.go:246 for production debugging (debug.Stack())
Extract magic number 100ms CPU sample interval in system_reader_linux.go:88 to a named constant
Consider adding a Reload() method to HookReloader interface so the /v1/hooks/reload endpoint triggers an actual filesystem rescan rather than just returning cached hooks

Wire FileSource in up.go: add file patterns to config, create FileSource instances, register with forwarder
Add HTTP status code checking to all CLI commands in actions.go and hooks.go
